Electric-Ensemble.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/electric-ensemble.html. That page is partly copied from the Tap Dancer manual and names the module 'Tap Dancer' in its Delay Line paragraph; the signal order it gives (saturation, two-pole low-pass with fixed resonance, delay taps, two-pole high-pass, mix) matches the arrows drawn on the Electric Ensemble panel, so it was used. The maker's input tooltips CV-Lp and CV-Hp were matched to the LP and HP knobs by panel position, not by index.

Tap-Dancer.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/tap-dancer.html. The panel prints LP twice (input filter and feedback tap), HP twice (feedback tap and output) and DUCK twice (feedback duck and output duck mix); the maker's own param names separate them and the panel positions were used to map them. Param 17 Feedback Amp has no panel lettering, only the arrow drawn back into the delay line. Param 20 In Mix also has no lettering and no artwork in the SVG: it is drawn in code as a three-position switch, and the binary carries the label 'Mid' beside 'In Mix' with 'Left' and 'Right' already present as port names, which suggests the three positions are left, mid and right. That was not confirmed, so the line says only that it is a three-position input mix. The Tap Dancer widget has a context menu with six items whose text could not be recovered from the binary; no Menu lines were written.

The signal fed into the saturator
The summed output of every saturated band
Thorns.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/thorns.html; it says only that the input is split into 8 bands, each saturated and then summed, with the band amplitudes drawn as a crown over the panel art. Param 1 Tone (panel TONE) has no line: no source says what it does to the bands, so it was left to fall back to the maker's tooltip. Its attenuverter and CV jack are described, because those are certain. The HQ line rests on the string 'Higher(4x)' in the binary, which sits between 'Tone' and 'Bands' in the Thorns block and reads as a four-times oversampling setting; the line does not quote the figure. The plugin is closed source, so no ranges could be confirmed for DRIVE, TONE or the band count.

Oppressor.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/oppressor.html, which describes the band splitting and nothing else. The plugin is closed source and the panel prints only SENSE, RANGE, A and R, so the SENSE and RANGE lines give the ordinary meanings of those controls on a ducker without a range or a threshold, which no source states. The module browser calls it a ducker and compressor; the manual calls it a multiband ducker, and the entry follows the manual.

Note — a track's meter is green when the file matches the engine sample rate, orange when the file was upsampled to reach it, and red when it was downsampled and high frequencies were thrown away
Menu — files are loaded one track at a time, or six at once from a folder, in WAV or FLAC; Unload All empties every track
Stems.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/stems.html. The transport buttons carry icons and no lettering; the maker's param names Stop, Play From Start, Play, Pause and Reset were used, and the panel positions confirm the left-to-right order. The manual gives the meter colours and the resampling behaviour but does not distinguish Stop from Pause, so neither line claims what happens to the play position. The time display and the track display are drawn in code and have no clickable control.

Prodigal-Son.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/prodigal-son.html, which gives the 14kHz to 20kHz band limit, the octave drop taking the band limit with it, the separate noise sustain and the chaos modulation by low-passed white noise. Param 15 Quality (panel Q) and param 16 Waveform (panel WF) have no lines: the binary carries the strings Digital Overdose, Saw and No Fundamentals in the Prodigal Son block, but which switch each belongs to could not be settled, so both were left to fall back to the maker's tooltips. Input 4 Note has no family: the panel pairs it with the NOTE knob the way the DETUNE and MIX jacks are paired with theirs, and there is already a separate V/O input at one volt per octave, so whether it is scaled per octave is unknown and no colour was given.

Prince-Of-Perception.notes: Manual read at https://flagaudio.com/vcv/prince-of-perception.html, which gives the 2ms to 20 seconds delay range, the 40 second scan, the -5V to 5V CV ranges, the sidechain normalling and every menu item. The manual calls the module Prism Of Perception twice in its own text, in the FRZ and SCN paragraphs; the panel and the plugin both say Prince Of Perception, and the entry follows the panel. The menu wording and the list of EOC divisions were confirmed against strings in the binary. Input 3 is declared in the code with no widget and no panel position, so it can never be clicked and has no line, tag or family.
